LESSON: WRITING 11.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it difficult to spell some words correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts
2. write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 11.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 11.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity

What this means
In this part you learn to write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling to a partner. (skill: write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts.
3. Practise this skill: write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it difficult to spell some words correctly?
2. How can we become better at spelling words?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify commonly misspelt words in oral and written contexts.
5. Be able to: write commonly misspelt words correctly for communication clarity.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
